events.name: FALLACY_UPDATED
events.description: The classification state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: fallacy classification, verdict, running score, argument card, informal fallacy

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: PICK_LABEL
events.description: Learner classified the current argument as valid or as a named fallacy; the first pick per item is verdicted and scored.

events.name: REVEAL_ANSWER
events.description: Learner asked for the answer and its explanation.

events.name: NEXT_ITEM
events.description: Learner advanced to the next argument card in the corpus.

default.explanation: It attacks the person rather than the argument — ad hominem.
default.hint: Does this engage the plan, or the person?
default.text: You're only against the plan because you never liked me.

default.explanation: It presents two extremes as the only possibilities — false dilemma.
default.hint: Are those really the only two options?
default.text: We either ban all cars or accept choking smog forever.

default.explanation: From P→Q and Q it concludes P — affirming the consequent.
default.hint: Can the match be cancelled for another reason?
default.text: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match is cancelled, so it rained.

default.explanation: It exaggerates the position into something easier to attack — straw man.
default.hint: Is that really what he argued?
default.text: He wants the library closed? Next he'll want books banned.

default.explanation: The conclusion follows necessarily from the premises — a valid argument.
default.hint: Does the conclusion follow from the premises?
default.text: All mammals breathe air. Whales are mammals, so whales breathe air.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Corpus
overridableConfigKeys.description: Argument cards (text, correct classification, hint, explanation) presented one at a time; the answer must be one of the fallacySet values.
overridableConfigKeys.synonyms: argument card, corpus, exercise set, fallacy example, argument

overridableConfigKeys.label: Correct Color
overridableConfigKeys.description: Box color of the correct label once revealed.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Fallacy Set
overridableConfigKeys.description: The classification labels offered as buttons and drawn as the canvas boxes; value is the machine key, label and color are what the learner sees.
overridableConfigKeys.synonyms: fallacy, ad hominem, straw man, false dilemma, affirming the consequent, informal fallacy, valid argument

overridableConfigKeys.label: Incorrect Color
overridableConfigKeys.description: Box color of a wrong selected label once revealed.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Interactive
overridableConfigKeys.description: Enable pointer interaction on the canvas.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Match Mode
overridableConfigKeys.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Pass Score
overridableConfigKeys.description: Number of correct classifications the learner is aiming for, shown next to the running score.
overridableConfigKeys.synonyms: mastery threshold, target score, passing grade

overridableConfigKeys.label: Show Hint
overridableConfigKeys.description: Show the current card's hint caption before the answer is revealed.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Shuffle
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, Next Argument advances by a stride of 3 through the corpus, interleaving cards instead of stepping linearly.
